artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: The ONE shipped file. C17's three bounds plus AMENDMENT 1's thread widening. The RUNNING bytes are the build input, not merely the right filename: SSM md5 of all 100 non-pycache files under /opt/opal-gateway/app against release commit 185dc04888 -- 100 EQUAL, 0 DIFFERENT, 0 release-only, 0 host-only, and this module reads d946f7fee327 on both sides. NEGATIVE CONTROL against the base d9f2ebded9: exactly 1 DIFFERENT, this file, which is precisely the payload -- so the instrument discriminates and the world moved by exactly one file.

Source-only and SHIPS NOWHERE -- test files are not executed on the host, which is why the negative control above isolates one changed file and not two. Four new tests cover the three bounds and the added basis field, and they assert on the CALLS rather than the response, because a handler that listed everything and filtered afterwards would return an identical body while saving nothing. The pre-C17 expectation that a superseded refusal still stands was split into two arms rather than quietly flipped.

acceptance.denominator: The SERVED module's own cold read, 8.2 s against the 10 s bar over 1,386 body fetches, with 4 of 4 boxes reading 'recorded'. Against the pre-C17 served figures of 22.8 s and 2,771 fetches, that is a 64 percent fall in time and a 50 percent fall in fetches.
acceptance.status_reason: Every clause met on the SERVED code, which is the only reading that settles the cell. Run from the main tree because the check shells out to a sibling probe that the release branch does not contain; AC3 is SERVED-scoped and reads nothing from HEAD, so the tree it runs from cannot change its measurement. THE MARGIN IS THIN AND IS NOT DRESSED UP: 8.2 s is 1.22x, and at about 5.9 ms per fetch the bar corresponds to roughly 1,690 fetches against today's 1,386 -- some 22 percent headroom in WINDOW POPULATION rather than in time, and that population grows through the working day (1,346 -> 1,371 -> 1,381 -> 1,386 across today's samples). The criterion is met; the problem is not retired.

mutant.description: The order names no mutant, so none is owed and none was run. In its place every discriminating read carried a NEGATIVE CONTROL, because a comparison that cannot fail is not evidence.
mutant.expected: n/a -- the spec names no mutant.
mutant.observed: Four controls fired and all four discriminated. (1) The live-base read: 100 of 100 app files equal d9f2ebded9, while the SAME instrument against the superseded 28ba9532b6 read 3 DIFFERENT -- OG-ap-10's payload -- so the base was established by content and the label was never relied on. (2) The post-act running-bytes read: 100 of 100 equal to the release, while the same comparison against the base read exactly 1 different, which is the one shipped file. (3) The rollback proof: the artifact equals the base commit and the host 100 of 100 in all three pairings, while the same artifact against the superseded base reads 3 different. (4) The cold probe's cache guard: cache_at_start was asserted and printed 0 on every sample, and a warm cache VOIDS the sample (rc=3) rather than reporting a fast one -- row Z-S32, where a module-level cache once made a second handler in the same process look 21x faster than its own mechanism allows.

determinism.method: The load condition was sampled five times across two bases and three wall-clock points, each a fresh interpreter with the cache asserted empty; AC1 and AC2 were run three times each (pre-commit, post-commit, and after AMENDMENT 1) and the issuer re-ran both independently in this seat's worktree; the tool surface was read twice through one reader; the running-bytes comparison was taken once over a complete 100-file denominator with a negative control.
determinism.observed: Stable within each population and directional where this cell moved the world. 16.661 s / 1,346 fetches before AMENDMENT 1, which STOPPED the cell at the bar; then 7.751 / 7.054 / 6.407 s at 1,371 on the old base; 7.899 s at 1,381 on the re-cut; 8.2 s at 1,386 served. TWO THINGS A READER SHOULD NOT TAKE AT FACE VALUE. First, the fetch count is not fixed: it rose monotonically through the day as the 48 h window filled, so every time figure here is relative to a population that was measured, not assumed -- the window held 2,134 records of 3,329 total history when counted directly at 09:48Z. Second, the three same-base samples fell monotonically at an identical fetch count and identical window contents, which means something outside the handler's own body cache warms between fresh interpreters; it is recorded without an explanation rather than explained away, and the WORST sample is the one carried against the bar in every case.

compiler_tools.result: PASS. The pattern file is written directly rather than through `git sparse-checkout set`, because MSYS rewrites a leading-slash pattern into an absolute Windows path and the re-include silently never applies -- a trap this seat hit on MP-r-2, where meeting_allowlist.json went missing while `sparse-checkout list` printed the mangled pattern as if in force. In a linked worktree `.git` is a FILE, so the naive .git/info path fails with 'Not a directory'.

compiler_tools.result: 62 passed / 0 failed, up from 58 by the four tests this cell added. The useful failure was my own: the first-seen bound test hardcoded 20 records against an 8-wide fetch chunk, and when AMENDMENT 1 raised FETCH_THREADS to 32 one chunk swallowed the fixture and the 'never fetched' assertion failed. The handler was right and the test was coupled to the constant -- it would have gone on passing while proving nothing. It now sizes its fixture from the module's own FETCH_THREADS and carries a positive control that the scan fetched anything at all.
